doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Lessons with Jake Hanna fixing his drum technique
summary: Jake Hanna corrected his grip and technique, and watching him play taught Smith tuning and setup.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I see you had some association with Jake Hanna early on.

Yes, sure did. Not too early really. I’d been playing quite a while before I took lessons from him. And my early studies were with a pretty generic drum teacher, who said you play a quarter note this way, and do this this way, and do that that way. But despite that he still told me some wrong techniques, and it took Jake Hanna to turn my technique around or I’d still be playing wrong.

I never played matched grip. But I didn’t have my left hand far enough over, like the old time drummers did. And that’s the first thing Jake Hanna said. “Nope, not far enough over.” “I can’t do that.” It took forever. But I’m glad. But I’ve picked up a lot — not so much from the lessons as just from watching him play, watching the techniques he uses and how he tunes the drums, and the height he sits, and where he has his equipment and all that. That was as useful to me as the lessons.
In fact I think we’re going to see him in a couple of weeks in Aspen.
I hope so. He’s an absolutely terrific player to play in any style band and make it sound better than it already does.
